info.desc: Vitalogy is the third studio album by the American alternative rock band Pearl Jam, released on November 22, 1994 through Epic Records. Pearl Jam wrote and recorded while touring behind its previous album Vs. (1993). The music on the record was more diverse than previous releases, and consists of aggressive rock songs, ballads, and several experimental tracks. Vitalogy was packaged in a booklet that replicated material from a 1920s medical book. The album was first released on vinyl record, followed by a release in other formats two weeks later on December 6, 1994. Upon its CD release, Vitalogy became the .

podcast.body: Pearl Jam released *Vitalogy* on vinyl two weeks before the CD edition, underscoring their love of old-school formats. Despite vinyl being near extinction in 1994, demand was so high that the vinyl edition sold 34,000 copies in its first week — a record for first-week vinyl sales until Jack White's *Lazaretto* sold 40,000 in one week in 2014. The opening song, "Spin the Black Circle," is an ode to vinyl itself. "Pearl Jam may have thought they were fighting against the future with the vinyl release of Vitalogy, but they were actually predicting it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album was notable for its vinyl version being released two full weeks ahead of its CD counterpart, specifically on November 22, 1994, while the CD followed on December 6, 1994. The vinyl edition sold a healthy 34,000 copies in its first week, setting a record for early vinyl sales that remained unbroken until Jack White's album "Lazaretto" in 2014. "When it came time to release their Vitalogy album back in 1994, they released a vinyl version of the album Two Full Weeks Before The CD, and it sold a healthy 34,000 copies in its first week."
